pdf_title: GOIO: Generative Oversampling Approach to Class Imbalance and Overlap of Tabular Data
srcdet: 18 real-world datasets said to come from repositories 'including' UCI and the imbalanced-learn Python package; no per-dataset source mapping is given. 5 artificial datasets generated from two multivariate Gaussians following ref [50] (4,000 samples, 25 features each).
imbalance_creation: Real-world: a target class (#T) is selected as the minority class for binary classification, given per dataset in Table I: 'minority' (native minority) for most; a single class for avila_0vs5/0vs6/0vs7 (5, 6, 7), optical_digits (8), page-blocks_0vs3 (3); thresholds for scene (>=1), abalone_15 (>=15), abalone_6 (<=15 as printed), wine_quality (<=4). Synthetic: positive-class proportion (#P = 2.5, 5, 10) and positive-class mean (#M) set to control imbalance and overlap.
split_protocol: stratified 5-fold cross-validation, repeated with ten random seeds, average reported
characteristics_table: yes (Table I; Table II for artificial datasets)
ir_definition: IR = Nmaj / Nmin, where Nmaj and Nmin represent the number of majority and minority class instances
notes: Tables I, II, V-VII are embedded as images (no extractable text); Table I and II were read from a rendered page image at PDF page index 7 (printed 6456). Dataset name 'taiwanses' is printed as is (likely typo). abalone_6 has #T printed as '<=15' (looks inconsistent with its name; copied as printed). Table I columns: Data Name, #T (target class), #F, #S, IR; Table II: Data Name, #M (positive mean), #P (positive proportion, %), #F, #S, IR. No per-dataset repository mapping. Model tokenizes numerical features by linear projection and categorical features by embedding lookup (p.6455), but no dataset-level encoding/normalisation/missing-value handling is described. UCI URL appears only in reference [48]. Drive folder is 'Both' but experiments are binary only; multiclass is future work. Five classifiers (GNB, KNN, DTC, SVM, RFC); experimental design follows [14].
